i  [llms.txt] llms.txt is a proposed format, not a standard: an H1 with the site name (the only required section), an optional summary in a blockquote, then H2 sections of links. Save it at /llms.txt.

i  [llms.txt] Google says: "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup to appear in these features" (AI Overviews and AI Mode). So llms.txt is optional, and not a lever for Google.

i  [-] Google says there is "no special schema.org structured data" needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode, and lists "making sure your structured data matches the visible text on the page" among the fundamentals.

cases.name: generate: home page off the root, vague title, no image
stdout: AAJ - STRUCTURED DATA, META TAGS AND LLMS.TXT (home page)
FIX BEFORE PUBLISHING - 2 issues to fix before you add this to the page.

!  [WebSite] WebSite markup belongs on the home page. Google: "The WebSite structured data must be on the home page of the site." Your URL is https://example.com/about; use it on https://example.com/.
!  [meta] "Home" is a vague title. Google advises against vague descriptors such as "Home" or "Profile".
-  [meta] No description was given, so no meta description was generated. Google: a good one "informs and interests users with a short, relevant summary of what a particular page is about."
-  [meta] No image was given. The Open Graph protocol lists og:image as a required property: "An image URL which should represent your object within the graph."
-  [Organization] No description. Google has no required Organization properties but recommends adding the relevant ones.
i  [-] No page text supplied, so nothing was checked against what readers see. Set "html" or "visibleText" to run those checks.

i  [-] Google says there is "no special schema.org structured data" needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode, and lists "making sure your structured data matches the visible text on the page" among the fundamentals.
